context: A uni student interviews a retired investigative journalist
purpose: Teach: 刑務所/徴収/独裁/妨害/騒動/偽装/偽造/言論

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 今日はインタビューさせていただき、ありがとうございます。長年、言論の自由を守るために闘ってこられたと伺いました。
lines.en: Thank you for letting me interview you today. I heard you spent years fighting to protect freedom of speech.
lines.style: Polite respectful student opening with humble formal tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやいや、大したことじゃないよ。ただ、当時は独裁政権まがいの空気があってね、記者として黙っていられなかっただけだ。
lines.en: Oh no, it wasn't much. But back then the atmosphere was almost like a dictatorship, and as a journalist I couldn't stay silent.
lines.style: Humble elder reflecting with gravitas and quiet conviction here.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 確か、ある大企業の文書偽造を暴いた時、相手から取材妨害も受けたんですよね？
lines.en: If I recall, when you exposed a major company's document forgery, you were also obstructed during your reporting, weren't you?
lines.style: Curious student probing with respectful but pointed follow-up question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、ひどかったよ。経費を不正に徴収していた幹部たちが、偽装工作までしてね。世論を二分する騒動になった。
lines.en: Yes, it was terrible. The executives who had been illegally collecting expenses even staged a cover-up. It became a scandal that split public opinion.
lines.style: Old journalist recounting battles with weary but steady firmness.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: その後、関係者の何人かは刑務所に収監されたと聞きました。先生は身の危険を感じませんでしたか？
lines.en: I heard several of those involved were later sent to prison. Didn't you fear for your own safety, sir?
lines.style: Serious student asking sensitive question with careful measured concern.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 怖くないと言えば嘘になる。脅迫電話もあったし、家の前で待ち伏せされたこともあった。でも、書くのをやめたら負けだからね。
lines.en: I'd be lying if I said I wasn't scared. There were threatening calls, and once they even waited outside my house. But if I'd stopped writing, I would have lost.
lines.style: Veteran sharing fear honestly while showing principled stubborn resolve.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 今の時代、SNSで偽造された画像や嘘の情報が一瞬で広がります。先輩としてアドバイスをいただけますか？
lines.en: These days, forged images and fake information spread instantly on social media. Could you give me some advice as a senior in the field?
lines.style: Earnest student seeking mentorship and connecting past to present.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 一次資料に当たること。それから、誰が得をするのか常に考えること。真実は地味だが、それを守るのが我々の仕事だよ。
lines.en: Always go to primary sources. And always ask who benefits. Truth is unglamorous, but protecting it is our job.
lines.style: Mentor delivering distilled wisdom with calm authoritative paternal warmth.
